case_title: Sumitha Pradeep v. Arun Kumar C.K & Anr.
accused_occupation: Advocate (as stated in the Sessions Court's order, recording the victim's counsel's submission)
evidence_type: Victim's statements (s.164 CrPC and to police and magistrate), medical examination, counselling records, school report
aggravating_circumstances: Accused is the victim's maternal uncle; victim aged 12; allegations of sexual assault; victim's academic performance adversely affected by trauma
trial_court_outcome: No trial held; Sessions Court declined anticipatory bail (order dated 4 July 2022)
high_court_outcome: Conditional anticipatory bail granted to accused (order dated 25 July 2022)
neutral_facts: The victim, a 12-year-old girl, is the niece of the accused, who is her maternal uncle. It is alleged that on 14 December 2021, at the accused's house where the victim and her mother had stayed for some days, the accused asked the victim to sit on his lap. He then hugged her, kissed her on the cheeks and tried to kiss her on the lips. It is alleged that he attempted to remove her top, touched her breasts and made sexual comments, and that the victim cried out, after which he released her. The allegations state that the incident occurred in an upstairs bedroom while no other person was present. The victim, previously an excellent student, afterwards declined markedly in her studies, with her grades falling from mostly A grades in sixth standard to mostly C grades in seventh standard. She was taken for counselling. In the first session she did not open up, and in the second session she disclosed the incident. She had not told her mother earlier, out of fear. The complaint was made about six months after the incident. A first information report was registered on 27 May 2022. A medical examination of the victim was conducted, and her statement under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was recorded. Her statements to the police and to a magistrate describe the incident. The counsellor's statement and the victim's school report form part of the material.
physical_harm: No physical injury stated; psychological trauma and decline in academic performance
number_of_offences: 7 charged; 0 finally upheld (no conviction; accused not tried)
key_evidence_accepted: Victim's s.164 CrPC statement, read with the FIR allegations, treated as supporting serious allegations (prima facie, for bail purposes)
witness_credibility: Not assessed; the Supreme Court expressly declined to express views on the merits
bail_history: Sessions Court refused anticipatory bail (4 July 2022); High Court granted conditional anticipatory bail (25 July 2022); Supreme Court set aside the High Court's grant
trial_duration: offence: 14-12-2021; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 25-07-2022; Supreme Court: 21-10-2022
legal_representation: Accused (respondent no.1): Raghenth Basant, Ms. Zehra Khan, Ajay Krishna, Harshad V. Hameed, Dileep Poolakkot, Mrs. Ashly Harshad. Appellant (victim's mother): Gaurav Agrawal, Ms. Anu K. Joy, Alim Anvar, Arvind Gupta. State: not separately shown
investigation_status: FIR registered (Crime No. 442 of 2022, 27 May 2022); medical examination and s.164 statement done; charge-sheet reportedly filed (per accused's counsel, not verified by Court)
procedural_irregularity: High Court's para 9 observations were unwarranted and overlooked FIR allegations; High Court appears not to have followed the binding coordinate-bench decision in Joy
appeal_history: Trial court (Sessions Court): anticipatory bail refused. High Court: anticipatory bail granted with conditions. Supreme Court: appeal by victim's mother allowed, High Court order set aside
prosecution_argument: High Court erred in granting anticipatory bail in a serious POCSO case; victim's trauma and academic decline; s.29 POCSO presumption; risk of interference with investigation
defence_argument: No custodial interrogation required; charge-sheet already filed; complaint retaliatory over property dispute (as put forward in the Sessions Court)
legal_principle_applied: Anticipatory bail: consider prima facie case first, then nature and severity of offence; absence of need for custodial interrogation alone is not a ground to grant bail; investigating officer should have free hand
precedent_relied_upon: Joy v. State of Kerala (2019) 1 KLT 935 (Kerala HC), on s.29 POCSO presumption and bail; referred to in the judgment
judicial_aggravating_factors: Victim's severe trauma and academic impact; legislative intent under s.29 POCSO; serious nature of allegations
other_sentence_order: High Court's anticipatory bail order set aside; Investigating Officer granted liberty to proceed in accordance with law
